description:
DECISION TICKET — needs the user.

## Current contract, verified at origin/main a3a9761d

fz's type system treats `pid` as an opaque nominal type, distinct from `integer`. Fresh probes confirm both cross-directions fail spec checking: `self()` cannot satisfy an `integer` parameter, and literal `1` cannot satisfy a `pid` parameter.

Kernel deliberately widens only the public send surface:

```fz
extern "C" fn fz_self() :: pid
extern "C" fn fz_send(pid, t) :: t when t: any

@doc "... receiver is a pid or its raw integer index ..."
@spec send(pid | integer, t) :: t when t: any
fn send(pid, msg), do: fz_send(pid, msg)
```

The runtime has no runtime pid tag. `fz_self_raw` returns `Process.pid as u64`; `fz_send_ref` casts the receiver word to `u32`, and the scheduler uses that number as the key in its task table. There is no named-process `register`/`whereis` API. `Process` exposes only `heap_alloc_stats/0`.

Therefore `send(1, msg)` works because Kernel explicitly accepts `integer` and the runtime treats it as a task index—not because pid rendering controls type compatibility.

## Existing route for replies

Captured pid threading already works:

```fz
fn main() do
  home = self()
  spawn(fn () -> send(home, 42) end)
  dbg(receive do x -> x end)
end
```

Both run and interp print `42`. A top-level zero-capture `spawn(&child/0)` has no enclosing value to capture, but that is not itself a missing runtime capability; callers can use a closure when the child needs context.

Exactly 15 fixture files still contain `send(1, ...)`, unchanged since 417c5b0b5. They rely on the deterministic root task index.

## Decision

Choose one coherent public contract:

A. Keep raw integer addressing as an intentional fz extension. Preserve `send(pid | integer, ...)`, document that `pid` remains nominal even though it renders/stores as an integer task index, and retain the fixtures.

B. Tighten `send/2` to nominal `pid`. Migrate all 15 fixtures to capture `home = self()` or otherwise thread an obtained pid, and add negative coverage proving arbitrary integers are rejected.

Named-process registration is a separate feature choice, not required to remove literal pid addressing. Changing spawn to inject a parent argument would also change its established zero-argument closure contract and should only be proposed separately.

## Signal

- Explicit tests pin pid/integer type disjointness.
- run/interp/build agree on captured-pid send/receive.
- Option A: raw integer send remains positively tested and documented.
- Option B: raw integer send fails type checking and no fixture contains `send(1, ...)`.
title: Decide whether send/2 accepts raw integer task indexes or only nominal pids
